assistant/config.py:
"""Settings read from environment variables, with safe defaults for local demos."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_KNOWLEDGE = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "knowledge")


def _parse_keys(raw: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """ASSISTANT_API_KEYS="key1:ana,key2:carla" -> {key: user_id}."""
    keys: dict[str, str] = {}
    for entry in filter(None, (part.strip() for part in raw.split(","))):
        key, sep, user = entry.partition(":")
        if not sep or not key or not user:
            raise ValueError(f"ASSISTANT_API_KEYS entry must be key:user_id, got {entry!r}")
        keys[key] = user
    return keys


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    knowledge_path: str = DEFAULT_KNOWLEDGE
    provider: str = "offline"  # offline | openai | anthropic | bedrock | ollama
    embedder: str = "hashing"  # hashing | openai | ollama | bedrock
    vector_store: str = "memory"  # memory | pinecone | weaviate
    llm_router: bool = False  # let the model pick graph intents (from a fixed menu)
    openai_model: str = "gpt-4o-mini"
    openai_embed_model: str = "text-embedding-3-small"
    anthropic_model: str = ""  # set ANTHROPIC_MODEL to an Anthropic model id
    bedrock_model: str = "amazon.nova-micro-v1:0"
    bedrock_embed_model: str = "amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0"
    aws_region: str = "us-east-1"
    ollama_url: str = "http://localhost:11434"
    ollama_model: str = "llama3.1"
    ollama_embed_model: str = "nomic-embed-text"
    top_k: int = 5
    abstain_below: float = 0.6  # minimum question coverage for an extractive answer
    min_support: float = 0.6  # minimum share of a sentence's words found in its cited passage
    audit_path: str = ""  # optional JSONL audit log file
    api_keys: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def auth_enabled(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.api_keys)


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    env = os.environ.get
    return Settings(
        knowledge_path=env("ASSISTANT_KNOWLEDGE_PATH", DEFAULT_KNOWLEDGE),
        provider=env("ASSISTANT_PROVIDER", "offline").lower(),
        embedder=env("ASSISTANT_EMBEDDER", "hashing").lower(),
        vector_store=env("ASSISTANT_VECTOR_STORE", "memory").lower(),
        llm_router=env("ASSISTANT_LLM_ROUTER", "false").lower() in {"1", "true", "yes"},
        openai_model=env("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini"),
        openai_embed_model=env("OPENAI_EMBED_MODEL", "text-embedding-3-small"),
        anthropic_model=env("ANTHROPIC_MODEL", ""),
        bedrock_model=env("BEDROCK_MODEL", "amazon.nova-micro-v1:0"),
        bedrock_embed_model=env("BEDROCK_EMBED_MODEL", "amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0"),
        aws_region=env("AWS_REGION", "us-east-1"),
        ollama_url=env("OLLAMA_URL", "http://localhost:11434").rstrip("/"),
        ollama_model=env("OLLAMA_MODEL", "llama3.1"),
        ollama_embed_model=env("OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL", "nomic-embed-text"),
        audit_path=env("ASSISTANT_AUDIT_PATH", ""),
        api_keys=_parse_keys(env("ASSISTANT_API_KEYS", "")),
    )
assistant/core.py:
"""The assistant: route a question, retrieve what the asker may use, answer, and verify.

    question ──► router ──► graph templates ─────────────┐
                   │                                     ├─► answer + citations + trace
                   └──► permission-aware hybrid search ──┤
                          └─► draft answer ─► grounding check (drop unsupported, or abstain)

`mode="naive"` turns every guardrail off (no access filter, no lifecycle filter, no
abstention, no grounding check). It exists only so the demo and the evaluation can show
what those guardrails prevent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import threading
import time
import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .config import Settings, get_settings
from .gateway import LLMProvider, get_embedder, get_provider
from .graph import MemoryGraph, explain
from .grounding import Source, extractive_answer, verify
from .knowledge import Document, KnowledgeBase, KnowledgeError, User
from .retrieval import AccessFilter, HybridRetriever, MemoryVectorStore, VectorStore
from .router import Route, route, route_with_llm
from .text import content_terms, tokenize

MODES = ("grounded", "naive")

ANSWER_SYSTEM = """You answer employee questions for Ridgeway Health using ONLY the numbered sources.
Rules:
- After every sentence, cite the source it came from in square brackets, like [2].
- Copy numbers, amounts, dates and time limits exactly as the source writes them.
- Do not add advice, background or anything the sources don't say.
- If the sources don't answer the question, reply with exactly: NOT_FOUND
- Answer in 1 to 3 short sentences."""

_CONTACT_WORDS = set(
    tokenize(
        "who should do can i ask contact talk call email reach out about with problems problem issues issue questions "
        "approved approve signed sign off owns own owner maintains responsible wrote"
    )
)


# Greetings, thanks and "what can you do?" aren't policy questions. Answering them with
# "I can't answer that" is unfriendly, and searching for them returns random passages.
_GREETING = re.compile(
    r"^(hi|hello|hey|hiya|howdy|yo|good (morning|afternoon|evening)|greetings)\b[\s!.,]*(there|team|all)?[\s!.]*$", re.I
)
_THANKS = re.compile(r"^(thanks|thank you|thx|ty|ok|okay|cool|great|got it|bye|goodbye)\b[\s!.,a-z]*$", re.I)
_HELP = re.compile(r"^(help|what can you do|what do you (do|know)|how does this work|who are you)\b[\s?!.]*$", re.I)


class NotFound(LookupError):
    pass


class Forbidden(PermissionError):
    pass


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _slug(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.lower()).strip("-")[:60] or "document"


class Assistant:
    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: Settings | None = None,
        kb: KnowledgeBase | None = None,
        vector_store: VectorStore | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.settings = settings or get_settings()
        root = Path(self.settings.knowledge_path)
        self.kb = kb or KnowledgeBase.load(root)
        self.graph = MemoryGraph(self.kb)
        self.retriever = HybridRetriever(self.kb, get_embedder(self.settings), vector_store or self._vector_store())
        suggestions = root / "suggestions.json"
        self.suggestions: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = (
            json.loads(suggestions.read_text()) if suggestions.exists() else {}
        )
        self.audit: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def _vector_store(self) -> VectorStore:
        if self.settings.vector_store == "pinecone":
            from .backends.pinecone import PineconeStore

            return PineconeStore.from_env()
        if self.settings.vector_store == "weaviate":
            from .backends.weaviate import WeaviateStore

            return WeaviateStore.from_env()
        return MemoryVectorStore()

    # ---------- helpers ----------

    def user(self, user_id: str) -> User:
        try:
            return self.kb.directory.user(user_id)
        except KnowledgeError as exc:
            raise NotFound(str(exc)) from exc

    def _log(self, actor: str, action: str, **detail: Any) -> None:
        event = {"at": _now(), "actor": actor, "action": action, **detail}
        with self._lock:
            self.audit.append(event)
            if self.settings.audit_path:
                Path(self.settings.audit_path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                with open(self.settings.audit_path, "a") as f:
                    f.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")

    def _person(self, user_id: str | None) -> dict[str, str] | None:
        if not user_id or user_id not in self.kb.directory.users:
            return None
        u = self.kb.directory.users[user_id]
        return {"id": u.id, "name": u.name, "title": u.title, "org": self.kb.directory.org_name(u.org)}

    def _doc_info(self, doc: Document, viewer: User) -> dict[str, Any]:
        info = doc.summary()
        info["owner"] = self._person(doc.owner)
        info["approved_by"] = self._person(doc.approved_by)
        info["org_name"] = self.kb.directory.org_name(doc.org)
        info["audience_names"] = [self.kb.directory.role_name(r) for r in doc.audience]
        info["policy"] = self.kb.decide(viewer, doc).reason  # ok | draft | archived | no_access
        return info

    # ---------- asking ----------

    def ask(self, user_id: str, question: str, mode: str = "grounded", provider: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        question = question.strip()
        if not question:
            raise ValueError("Question is empty")
        if len(question) > 1000:
            raise ValueError("Question is too long (1000 characters max)")
        if mode not in MODES:
            raise ValueError(f"mode must be one of {MODES}")
        asker = self.user(user_id)
        guarded = mode == "grounded"
        llm = get_provider(provider or self.settings.provider, self.settings)
        flt = AccessFilter(tuple(asker.roles) if guarded else None)
        candidates = [d.id for d in self.kb.docs.values() if not guarded or self.kb.decide(asker, d).allowed]

        chat = self._small_talk(question, asker)
        if chat is not None:
            return chat

        if llm is not None and self.settings.llm_router:
            rt = route_with_llm(llm, question, asker, self.kb, candidates)
        else:
            rt = route(question, asker, self.kb, candidates)

        result: dict[str, Any] = {
            "id": f"ask_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]}",
            "user": self._person(asker.id),
            "question": question,
            "mode": mode,
            "provider": llm.name if llm else "offline",
            "route": rt.__dict__,
            "answer": "",
            "abstained": False,
            "citations": [],
            "graph": None,
            "trace": {"retrieved": [], "excluded": {}, "confidence": None, "verification": [], "draft": ""},
        }
        if rt.kind == "documents":
            self._answer_from_documents(result, asker, question, flt, llm, guarded)
        else:
            self._answer_from_graph(result, asker, question, rt, flt, guarded)

        result["latency_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 1)
        self._log(
            asker.id,
            "ask",
            question=question,
            mode=mode,
            route=rt.kind,
            abstained=result["abstained"],
            cited=sorted({c["doc_id"] for c in result["citations"]}),
        )
        return result

    def _small_talk(self, question: str, asker: User) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        """A friendly reply for greetings, thanks and "help", or None for real questions.
        Text with no searchable words at all ("???", "hmm") is treated as small talk too."""
        q = question.strip()
        if _THANKS.match(q):
            text = "You're welcome! Ask me anything else about Ridgeway Health's policies and procedures."
        elif _GREETING.match(q) or _HELP.match(q) or not content_terms(q):
            topics = sorted({d.title for d in self.kb.docs.values() if self.kb.decide(asker, d).allowed})
            listed = ", ".join(topics[:-1]) + f" and {topics[-1]}" if len(topics) > 1 else "".join(topics)
            text = (
                f"Hi {asker.name.split()[0]}! I answer questions about Ridgeway Health's policies and procedures, "
                f"using only approved documents you're allowed to read, and I cite every answer. "
                f"You can ask about the {listed}"
                + (", or relationship questions like who owns a policy or who you report to." if topics else ".")
            )
        else:
            return None
        self._log(asker.id, "ask", question=q, mode="chat", route="chat", abstained=False, cited=[])
        return {
            "id": f"ask_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]}",
            "user": self._person(asker.id),
            "question": q,
            "mode": "grounded",
            "provider": "offline",
            "route": {
                "kind": "chat",
                "intent": None,
                "params": {},
                "reason": "Greeting or small talk, not a policy question",
                "by": "rules",
            },
            "answer": text,
            "abstained": False,
            "citations": [],
            "graph": None,
            "trace": {"retrieved": [], "excluded": {}, "confidence": None, "verification": [], "draft": ""},
            "latency_ms": 0.0,
        }

    def _retrieve(self, result: dict[str, Any], asker: User, question: str, flt: AccessFilter) -> list[Source]:
        hits = self.retriever.search(question, flt, k=self.settings.top_k)
        sources = []
        for n, h in enumerate(hits, 1):
            c, doc = self.kb.chunks[h.chunk_id], self.kb.docs[h.doc_id]
            sources.append(Source(n, c.id, doc.id, doc.title, c.heading, c.text))
            result["trace"]["retrieved"].append(
                {
                    "n": n,
                    "chunk_id": c.id,
                    "doc_id": doc.id,
                    "title": doc.title,
                    "version": doc.version,
                    "heading": c.heading,
                    "score": h.score,
                    "bm25_rank": h.bm25_rank,
                    "vector_rank": h.vector_rank,
                    "policy": self.kb.decide(asker, doc).reason,
                }
            )
        if flt.active:
            # What the filter kept out, among passages this person can read. Passages they
            # can't read are not counted: even their existence is not disclosed.
            excluded: dict[str, int] = {}
            for h in self.retriever.search(question, AccessFilter(None), k=self.settings.top_k):
                reason = self.kb.decide(asker, self.kb.docs[h.doc_id]).reason
                if reason in {"draft", "archived"}:
                    excluded[reason] = excluded.get(reason, 0) + 1
            result["trace"]["excluded"] = excluded
        return sources

    def _cite(self, asker: User, src: Source, n: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
        doc = self.kb.docs[src.doc_id]
        return {
            "n": n,
            "kind": "passage",
            "chunk_id": src.chunk_id,
            "doc_id": doc.id,
            "title": doc.title,
            "version": doc.version,
            "status": doc.status,
            "heading": src.heading,
            "text": src.text,
            "owner": self._person(doc.owner),
            "policy": self.kb.decide(asker, doc).reason,
        }

    def _answer_from_documents(
        self,
        result: dict[str, Any],
        asker: User,
        question: str,
        flt: AccessFilter,
        llm: LLMProvider | None,
        guarded: bool,
    ) -> None:
        sources = self._retrieve(result, asker, question, flt)
        trace = result["trace"]
        if not sources:
            self._abstain(result, asker, "No passage you can use matches this question.")
            return
        if llm is None:
            draft, confidence = extractive_answer(question, sources, self.retriever.idf_of)
            trace["confidence"] = confidence
            if guarded and confidence < self.settings.abstain_below:
                trace["draft"] = draft
                self._abstain(result, asker, "The closest passages don't answer the question.", sources)
                return
        else:
            context = "\n\n".join(f"[{s.n}] {s.title} — {s.heading}: {s.text}" for s in sources)
            draft = llm.complete(ANSWER_SYSTEM, f"Sources:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {question}").strip()
            if "NOT_FOUND" in draft:
                trace["draft"] = draft
                if guarded:
                    self._abstain(result, asker, "The model found no answer in the sources.", sources)
                    return
        trace["draft"] = draft
        check = verify(draft, sources, self.settings.min_support)
        trace["verification"] = [v.__dict__ for v in check.verdicts]
        if guarded:
            if not check.kept:
                self._abstain(result, asker, "No sentence of the draft answer was supported by its sources.", sources)
                return
            kept = check.kept
        else:
            kept = check.verdicts  # naive: whatever the draft said, verified or not
        by_n = {s.n: s for s in sources}
        renumber: dict[int, int] = {}
        parts = []
        for v in kept:
            cites = []
            for c in v.cites:
                if c in by_n:
                    renumber.setdefault(c, len(renumber) + 1)
                    cites.append(renumber[c])
            parts.append(v.sentence + "".join(f" [{c}]" for c in cites))
        result["answer"] = " ".join(parts) if parts else draft
        result["citations"] = [self._cite(asker, by_n[old], new) for old, new in renumber.items()]

    def _answer_from_graph(
        self, result: dict[str, Any], asker: User, question: str, rt: Route, flt: AccessFilter, guarded: bool
    ) -> None:
        params = {**rt.params, "roles": list(asker.roles), "guarded": guarded}
        intent = rt.intent or ""
        if "topic" in rt.params:  # find the document by search first, then ask the graph about it
            sources = self._retrieve(result, asker, question, flt)
            topic = [t for t in content_terms(question) if t not in _CONTACT_WORDS]
            best = None
            for s in sources:
                toks = set(tokenize(f"{s.title} {s.heading} {s.text}"))
                total = sum(self.retriever.idf_of(t) for t in topic) or 1.0
                cov = sum(self.retriever.idf_of(t) for t in topic if t in toks) / total
                if best is None or cov > best[0]:
                    best = (cov, s)
            result["trace"]["confidence"] = round(best[0], 3) if best else 0.0
            if not best or (guarded and best[0] < self.settings.abstain_below):
                self._abstain(
                    result, asker, "No document you can use covers this topic, so there's no owner to point to."
                )
                return
            if intent == "topic_contact":
                intent = "doc_owner"
                params = {**params, "doc_id": best[1].doc_id, "topic": True}
            else:
                params = {**params, "doc_id": best[1].doc_id, "topic": False}
        rows = self.graph.run(intent, params)
        answer = explain(intent, params, rows, self.kb)
        result["graph"] = answer.as_dict()
        if not rows:
            self._abstain(result, asker, "The knowledge graph has no answer you have access to.")
            return
        result["answer"] = answer.text
        for i, doc_id in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(answer.doc_ids), 1):
            doc = self.kb.docs[doc_id]
            result["citations"].append(
                {
                    "n": i,
                    "kind": "graph",
                    "doc_id": doc.id,
                    "title": doc.title,
                    "version": doc.version,
                    "status": doc.status,
                    "owner": self._person(doc.owner),
                    "policy": self.kb.decide(asker, doc).reason,
                }
            )

    def _abstain(self, result: dict[str, Any], asker: User, why: str, sources: list[Source] | None = None) -> None:
        result["abstained"] = True
        result["trace"]["abstain_reason"] = why
        text = "I can't answer that from the approved documents you have access to."
        # Point to a person only when an allowed document is clearly on the same topic.
        if sources and (result["trace"].get("confidence") or 0) >= 0.4:
            doc = self.kb.docs[sources[0].doc_id]
            owner = self._person(doc.owner)
            if owner and self.kb.decide(asker, doc).allowed:
                text += f" The closest document is the {doc.title}; its owner, {owner['name']} ({owner['org']}), may be able to help."
        result["answer"] = text
        result["citations"] = []

    # ---------- knowledge management ----------

    def documents(self, user_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        viewer = self.user(user_id)
        return [self._doc_info(d, viewer) for d in self.kb.visible_docs(viewer)]

    def document(self, user_id: str, doc_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        viewer = self.user(user_id)
        doc = self.kb.docs.get(doc_id)
        if not doc or doc not in self.kb.visible_docs(viewer):
            raise NotFound("Document not found")  # same answer whether it exists or not
        info = self._doc_info(doc, viewer)
        info["body"] = doc.body
        info["chunks"] = [c.__dict__ for c in self.kb.chunks.values() if c.doc_id == doc_id]
        return info

    def add_document(
        self, user_id: str, title: str, body: str, audience: list[str], supersedes: str | None = None
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        author = self.user(user_id)
        title, body = title.strip(), body.strip()
        if not title or not body:
            raise ValueError("Title and text are required")
        version = 1
        if supersedes:
            old = self.kb.docs.get(supersedes)
            if not old or old not in self.kb.visible_docs(author):
                raise NotFound("The document to replace was not found")
            version = old.version + 1
        base = f"{_slug(title)}-v{version}"
        doc_id, i = base, 2
        while doc_id in self.kb.docs:
            doc_id, i = f"{base}-{i}", i + 1
        doc = Document(
            id=doc_id,
            title=title,
            version=version,
            status="draft",
            owner=author.id,
            org=author.org,
            audience=audience or ["employee"],
            effective=datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat(),
            body=body if body.startswith("#") or "\n## " in body else f"## {title}\n{body}",
            supersedes=supersedes,
        )
        try:
            with self._lock:
                self.kb.add(doc)
        except KnowledgeError as exc:
            raise ValueError(str(exc)) from exc
        self._log(author.id, "add_document", doc_id=doc.id, supersedes=supersedes)
        return self._doc_info(doc, author)

    def approve(self, user_id: str, doc_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        approver = self.user(user_id)
        doc = self.kb.docs.get(doc_id)
        if not doc or doc not in self.kb.visible_docs(approver):
            raise NotFound("Document not found")
        if not approver.is_admin:
            raise Forbidden("Only knowledge admins can approve documents")
        if doc.owner == approver.id:
            raise Forbidden("Owners can't approve their own documents; ask another knowledge admin")
        try:
            with self._lock:
                self.kb.approve(doc_id, approver.id)
        except KnowledgeError as exc:
            raise ValueError(str(exc)) from exc
        self._log(approver.id, "approve", doc_id=doc_id, archived=doc.supersedes)
        return self._doc_info(doc, approver)

    def graph_snapshot(self, user_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return self.graph.snapshot(self.user(user_id))

    def users(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        out = []
        for uid in self.kb.directory.demo_users:
            u = self.kb.directory.users[uid]
            out.append(
                {
                    **(self._person(uid) or {}),
                    "roles": [self.kb.directory.role_name(r) for r in u.roles if r != "employee"],
                    "admin": u.is_admin,
                    "suggestions": self.suggestions.get(uid, []),
                }
            )
        return out

    def evaluate(self, provider: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        from .evaluation import run_eval

        return run_eval(self, provider)
assistant/evaluation.py:
"""Evaluation: run the same questions with guardrails on and off, and score both.

Each case says who asks, what they ask, and either the facts a correct answer contains or
that the right answer is to abstain. Errors are classified automatically from the citations
and the access policy, so nobody has to label them by hand:

    leak          used a passage the asker isn't allowed to read
    draft         used an unapproved draft
    stale         used an archived or superseded version
    unsupported   answered a question the knowledge base can't answer
    wrong         answered, cited allowed sources, but missed the expected facts
    over_abstain  said "I don't know" when an allowed answer existed

The first four are grounding errors: the answer isn't backed by current knowledge the
asker may see. That's the number the guardrails exist to bring down.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .core import Assistant

GROUNDING_ERRORS = ("leak", "draft", "stale", "unsupported")
OUTCOMES = ("correct", "correct_abstain", *GROUNDING_ERRORS, "wrong", "over_abstain")


def load_cases(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return json.loads(path.read_text())["cases"]


def _norm(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(text.lower().replace("°", "°").split())


def judge(assistant: Assistant, case: dict[str, Any], result: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    asker = assistant.user(case["user"])
    expect_abstain = case.get("abstain", False)
    if result["abstained"]:
        return "correct_abstain" if expect_abstain else "over_abstain"
    reasons = {assistant.kb.decide(asker, assistant.kb.docs[c["doc_id"]]).reason for c in result["citations"]}
    for r in ("no_access", "draft", "archived"):
        if r in reasons:
            return {"no_access": "leak", "draft": "draft", "archived": "stale"}[r]
    if expect_abstain:
        return "unsupported"
    answer = _norm(result["answer"])
    if all(_norm(fact) in answer for fact in case.get("expect", [])):
        return "correct"
    return "wrong"


def _summary(outcomes: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    n = len(outcomes) or 1
    counts = {o: outcomes.count(o) for o in OUTCOMES}
    grounding = sum(counts[o] for o in GROUNDING_ERRORS)
    good = counts["correct"] + counts["correct_abstain"]
    return {
        "cases": len(outcomes),
        "counts": counts,
        "accuracy": round(good / n, 3),
        "grounding_errors": grounding,
        "grounding_error_rate": round(grounding / n, 3),
    }


def run_eval(
    assistant: Assistant, provider: str | None = None, cases: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if cases is None:
        cases = load_cases(Path(assistant.settings.knowledge_path) / "eval.json")
    rows = []
    for case in cases:
        row: dict[str, Any] = {k: case.get(k) for k in ("id", "user", "question", "category", "expect", "abstain")}
        for mode in ("naive", "grounded"):
            res = assistant.ask(case["user"], case["question"], mode=mode, provider=provider)
            row[mode] = {
                "outcome": judge(assistant, case, res),
                "answer": res["answer"],
                "abstained": res["abstained"],
                "route": res["route"]["kind"],
                "cited": [f"{c['doc_id']}" for c in res["citations"]],
            }
        rows.append(row)
    naive = _summary([r["naive"]["outcome"] for r in rows])
    grounded = _summary([r["grounded"]["outcome"] for r in rows])
    before, after = naive["grounding_errors"], grounded["grounding_errors"]
    return {
        "provider": provider or assistant.settings.provider,
        "naive": naive,
        "grounded": grounded,
        "grounding_error_reduction": round((before - after) / before, 3) if before else 0.0,
        "rows": rows,
    }


def to_markdown(report: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    n, g = report["naive"], report["grounded"]
    labels = {
        "correct": "Correct answer",
        "correct_abstain": 'Correctly said "I don\'t know"',
        "leak": "Leaked restricted content",
        "draft": "Used an unapproved draft",
        "stale": "Used an outdated version",
        "unsupported": "Made up an answer",
        "wrong": "Wrong answer",
        "over_abstain": 'Said "I don\'t know" but could have answered',
    }
    lines = [
        f"# Evaluation results ({report['provider']} provider)",
        "",
        f"{n['cases']} questions, asked as {len({r['user'] for r in report['rows']})} different employees. Generated by `gra eval --markdown`.",
        "",
        "| | Naive RAG | Grounded |",
        "|---|---:|---:|",
        f"| **Accuracy** | {n['accuracy']:.0%} | {g['accuracy']:.0%} |",
        f"| **Grounding errors** | {n['grounding_errors']} ({n['grounding_error_rate']:.0%}) | {g['grounding_errors']} ({g['grounding_error_rate']:.0%}) |",
    ]
    for key, label in labels.items():
        lines.append(f"| {label} | {n['counts'][key]} | {g['counts'][key]} |")
    lines += [
        "",
        f"Grounding errors fell by **{report['grounding_error_reduction']:.0%}** with guardrails on.",
        "",
        "## Per question",
        "",
        "| # | Asked by | Question | Naive | Grounded |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in report["rows"]:
        lines.append(
            f"| {r['id']} | {r['user']} | {r['question']} | {r['naive']['outcome']} | {r['grounded']['outcome']} |"
        )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

"""Text utilities shared by retrieval, answering and grounding checks."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

STOPWORDS = frozenset(
    """a an and are as at be been but by can could do does for from had has have he her his i if in into
    is it its me my no not of on or our she so than that the their them then there these they this to
    too up us was we were what when where which who whom will with would you your just also very really
    how many much should get per any am i'm im about tell please need know there's what's each every""".split()
)

_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:[.'][a-z0-9]+)*")
_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\$?\d+(?:[.,]\d+)*%?")
# A sentence ends at . ! or ? followed by a capital, digit, quote or $; a following "[n]"
# citation stays attached to the sentence before it, and the next sentence starts after it.
_SENTENCE = re.compile(r"(?:(?<=[.!?])|(?<=\]))\s+(?=[A-Z0-9\"'($])")
_CITE = re.compile(r"\s*\[(\d+)\]")

# A few domain synonyms so short questions still reach the right passages
# ("vacation" -> PTO). Real deployments get this from dense embeddings.
SYNONYMS = {
    "vacation": "pto",
    "daily": "day",
    "reimburse": "reimburs",
    "reimbursed": "reimburs",
    "reimbursement": "reimburs",
    "reimbursable": "reimburs",
    "2fa": "multi-factor",
    "mfa": "multi-factor",
    "fridge": "refrigerator",
    "temp": "temperature",
    "sev1": "sev1",
    "keep": "retain",
    "kept": "retain",
    "retained": "retain",
    "retention": "retain",
}


def stem(word: str) -> str:
    for suffix in ("ations", "ation", "ings", "ing", "ies", "edly", "ed", "es", "s"):
        if word.endswith(suffix) and len(word) - len(suffix) >= 3:
            return word[: -len(suffix)] + ("y" if suffix == "ies" else "")
    return word


def tokenize(text: str) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for w in _WORD.findall(text.lower()):
        if w in STOPWORDS or len(w) < 2:
            continue
        w = SYNONYMS.get(w, w)
        out.append(stem(w))
    return out


# Words that frame a question ("what is the meal *limit*", "how *long*") but rarely appear
# in the passage that answers it. They still drive retrieval; they don't count against coverage.
FRAME_WORDS = frozenset(
    stem(w)
    for w in "limit rate range long often quick quickly fast amount maximum minimum number allowed rule rules required requirement".split()
)


def content_terms(question: str) -> list[str]:
    """Question terms that an answering passage should contain (no frame words, no bare numbers)."""
    return [t for t in tokenize(question) if t not in FRAME_WORDS and not t.replace(".", "").isdigit()]


def numbers(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Numbers, money and percentages, normalised so "$75" and "75" compare equal."""
    return {n.strip("$%").replace(",", "") for n in _NUMBER.findall(text)}


def split_sentences(text: str) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for para in re.split(r"\n\s*\n|\n(?=#)", text):
        para = " ".join(line.strip() for line in para.splitlines() if not line.strip().startswith("#")).strip()
        if para:
            out.extend(s.strip() for s in _SENTENCE.split(para) if s.strip())
    return out


def strip_citations(sentence: str) -> tuple[str, list[int]]:
    cites = [int(n) for n in _CITE.findall(sentence)]
    return _CITE.sub("", sentence).strip(), cites


def chunk_markdown(body: str, max_words: int = 90) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Split a markdown body into (section heading, text) chunks.

    Chunks follow `##` sections so a passage never mixes two topics. Long sections are
    split on sentence boundaries. The heading is kept so the chunk reads on its own.
    """
    sections: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = [("", [])]
    for line in body.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("## "):
            sections.append((line[3:].strip(), []))
        elif line.startswith("# "):
            continue
        else:
            sections[-1][1].append(line)
    chunks: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for heading, lines in sections:
        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", " ".join(lines)).strip()
        if not text:
            continue
        current: list[str] = []
        count = 0
        for sentence in _SENTENCE.split(text):
            n = len(sentence.split())
            if current and count + n > max_words:
                chunks.append((heading, " ".join(current)))
                current, count = [], 0
            current.append(sentence)
            count += n
        if current:
            chunks.append((heading, " ".join(current)))
    return chunks

# Data Retention Policy

## Patient records
Patient medical records are retained for 10 years after the patient's last visit. Records for minors are retained until the patient turns 28.

## Email
Business email is retained for 3 years and then deleted automatically, unless it is under a legal hold.

## Audit logs
System audit logs are retained for 6 years.

## Legal holds
When a legal hold is issued, the Compliance Officer notifies the affected teams, and no covered data may be deleted until the hold is released.

---
# Patient Intake Procedure

## Identity check
Confirm every patient's identity with two identifiers, full name and date of birth, before any care is given. Never use the room number as an identifier.

## Allergies and medications
Review allergies and current medications at every visit, even if the patient was seen recently. Record "no known allergies" explicitly rather than leaving the field blank.

## Vital signs
Take and record vital signs within 15 minutes of rooming the patient. Repeat blood pressure after 5 minutes if the first reading is above 140/90.

## Language access
Offer a qualified medical interpreter to any patient who prefers a language other than English. Family members should not interpret clinical information.

# Paid Time Off Policy

## Accrual
Full-time employees accrue 20 days of paid time off (PTO) per calendar year. PTO covers vacation and personal days. Part-time employees accrue PTO in proportion to their scheduled hours.

## Carryover
Employees may carry over up to 5 unused PTO days into the next calendar year. Any unused days above 5 expire on December 31.

## Requesting time off
Submit PTO requests in the HR portal at least 2 weeks in advance. Your manager approves or declines the request within 3 business days. Requests during the December holiday period are approved in the order they are received.

## Sick leave
Sick leave is separate from PTO. Full-time employees receive 10 days of paid sick leave per year, and a doctor's note is required after 3 consecutive sick days.

---
# Vaccine Refrigerator Monitoring

## Temperature range
Vaccine refrigerators must stay between 2°C and 8°C. Check and log the temperature twice a day, at opening and at closing.

## Out-of-range readings
If a reading is outside 2°C to 8°C, label the vaccines "do not use", keep them refrigerated, and notify the pharmacy within 1 hour. Do not discard vaccines until the pharmacy confirms they are no longer viable.

## Power outages
During a power outage, keep the refrigerator door closed and move vaccines to the backup unit if the outage lasts longer than 2 hours.

# VPN and Multi-Factor Authentication Guide

## Setting up multi-factor authentication
Install the Microsoft Authenticator app on your phone and scan the QR code shown at first sign-in. Text message codes are not allowed for staff accounts.

## Connecting to the VPN
Use the GlobalProtect VPN client to reach internal systems from outside the clinic network. The VPN disconnects after 12 hours and you must sign in again.

## Lost phone or locked account
If you lose your phone or are locked out, call the IT service desk at extension 4357. The service desk verifies your identity before resetting multi-factor authentication.
